user: And what are the typical timelines?
answer:
The published review targets are:

- **10 business days** for card reason codes
- **20 business days** for transfer reason codes
- **Up to 45 calendar days** for complex cases involving a foreign acquirer. You are notified if your case falls into this category.

Your case is dispute 1 on TX-0401, a 240.00 EUR duplicate charge, which is currently open. The knowledge base does not say whether duplicate charges count as card or transfer reason codes. My earlier statement that the 10-business-day target would normally apply was an inference, not something the documentation confirms. So I can't tell you which target applies to your case.

The 10-day and 20-day figures are review targets, not guaranteed deadlines. I can't see the status of your case from my side. For a confirmed timeline or case updates, I can escalate your case to a human agent. Would you like me to do that?

Dispute handling process
## Review timelines
The review target is 10 business days for card reason codes and 20 business
days for transfer reason codes. Complex cases involving a foreign acquirer may
run to 45 calendar days; the customer is notified when that happens.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Complaints
## Acknowledgement and resolution
A complaint is acknowledged within one business day and resolved within 15
business days. Complex complaints may take up to 35 business days, with the
customer informed of the delay.

Customer security policy
## Card blocking
A customer may block a card immediately. Blocking is reversible for 30 days;
after that a replacement card must be ordered.
